# local 0013: The value of an assignment has the type of the right operand when the two types differ in signedness only

- Category: [Fixes](../../fix.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17228
- Recommended action: Apply the patch. It does not change the separate fault under Related, in which a volatile right operand is read once per use.
- Patch: [local-0013.patch](../../patches/local-0013.patch), commit [`743f4d166`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/743f4d166d03fb63069ca1a8538b436ebc6b0f33). Applies to r17228 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The value of an assignment expression is the value of the left operand after the assignment, and
it has the type of the left operand (C11 6.5.16). When the types of the two operands differ in
signedness only, SDCC uses the right operand with its own type as the value, and the expression
that uses the value converts it with the wrong signedness. The file below was compiled with
`sdcc -mmcs51 --model-large asgn.c` on r17200 with the earlier patches of this report, and run in
ucsim.

```c
volatile unsigned char vu;
signed char sc = -1;
signed char gs;
unsigned char uc = 200;
int i;

__xdata __at (0x7000) unsigned char res[4];

void main (void)
{
  i = vu = sc;                  /* 255 */
  res[0] = i;
  res[1] = i >> 8;
  i = gs = uc;                  /* -56 */
  res[2] = i;
  res[3] = i >> 8;
  for (;;);
}
```

After the run `res` holds `ff ff c8 00`, and `ff 00 c8 ff` is expected. Without `--model-large` it
holds `ff ff c8 ff`.

A test of 84 assertions, which is not part of the patch, shows the extent. 52 of them fail for
mcs51-small, stm8, and ucz80, and 54 for mcs51-large. The value is wrong for the widths 8, 16, and
32 bits. It is wrong for left operands that are volatile objects, local variables, parameters,
array elements, struct members, and objects accessed through a pointer. Of these four targets,
only mcs51-large gives a wrong value for a global left operand that is not volatile, as in the
second assignment above. The right operand can be a variable or a constant of the other
signedness, and `i = vu = -1` gives -1. Compound assignments whose result before the store has
the other signedness are wrong too, such as `i = (vu += sc)`. Each use in which the signedness
matters is wrong: a conversion to a wider type, a comparison, a division, a right shift, a
function argument, and a return value. With `unsigned char *p` and `signed char *ps`,
`i = *(p = ps)` sign-extends for a local or volatile `p`, and the assignment gets warning 244.
Bit-fields, `_Bool`, and the conditional operator are correct.

## Cause

`compareType` returns -2 for two types that differ in signedness only, and `checkTypes` in
`src/SDCCicode.c` casts the right operand for -1 only. `geniCodeAssign` then returns the right
operand with its own type as the value of the assignment. For a global left operand that is not
volatile, `geniCodeAssign` returns an iTemp of the left type, which is assigned the right operand
without a cast. For mcs51 with `--model-large`, a pass between the iCode dumps `genconstprop_1`
and `genconstprop_2` replaces that iTemp by the right operand. The pass was not identified.

## Fix

In `ast2iCode` in `src/SDCCicode.c`, the case of `=` returns a cast of the right operand to the
type of the left operand, without `volatile` and `_Atomic`, when `compareType` gives -2 for the
two types and the left operand is not a bit-field. The cast follows the assignment, so the iCode
of the assignment does not change, and `killDeadCode` removes the cast when the value is not
used. A volatile right operand is cast before the assignment, so that it is read once.
`checkTypes` and `geniCodeAssign` are unchanged. A cast in `checkTypes` would replace the
assignment by a `CAST` iCode in each assignment between types of different signedness, also where
the value is not used.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/assignment-value.c` has 32 assertions. On r17200 with the earlier
patches of this report, 25 of them fail for mcs51-small, stm8, and ucz80, and 27 for mcs51-large
and mcs51-large-stack-auto. With the patch the test passes on host, stm8, ucz80, and six mcs51
variants: the small, medium, large, and huge models, and `--stack-auto` with the small and large
models. The test disables warning 158, because some of its constants do not fit in the left
operand. With this patch and the patch for bug #3986, the file above gives `ff 00 c8 ff` with and
without `--model-large`.

With the patch, the regression suite has 0 failures for mcs51-small, mcs51-large, and stm8, and
the diagnostics suite has 0 failures for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8. With
the patch for bug #3986 added, the regression suite has 0 failures for the nine targets above.
The other ports were not built.

The assembly of one other regression test differs. `gcc-torture-execute-990222-1.c` has
`(*--ptr += 1) > '9'` with a plain `char`, which is unsigned. The comparison was signed, which is
wrong for a sum above 127, and it is unsigned with the patch. The code is 7 bytes smaller for the
six mcs51 variants and 6 bytes smaller for ucz80, and for stm8 `jrsle` becomes `jrule`. The
library assembly files are identical with and without the patch for the six mcs51 models, stm8,
stm8-large, and z80. Assignments whose value is not used compile to the same code.

## Related

- The patch for bug #3986 requires this patch. With that patch alone, `i = s = 100 + 100` for a
  volatile signed char `s` sets `i` to 200. The test has this statement and expects -56.
- A separate fault is present with and without the patch. When the right operand is a volatile
  object of the type of the left operand and the value of the assignment is used, the code reads
  the right operand once for each use. For mcs51-small, `i = vs8b = vs8` with two volatile
  `signed char` objects reads `vs8` three times. The entry local 0014 describes this fault and has
  a patch for it.
